page: Microsoft Azure E32ads_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Eadsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 1890 GB NVMe SSD and is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present on this server type.

Benchmark data highlights exceptional single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-threaded performance is also robust, as evidenced by a strong (top 25%) rating in the PassMark CPU score, CPU extended instructions, and CPU encryption tests. However, multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng and database operations fall into the average (middle 50%) category. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes also register in the average tier.

This instance is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and single-threaded processing tasks. While it demonstrates strong capabilities in small-scale LLM inference, achieving top-tier text generation speeds for a 135M parameter model, it exhibits a significant performance tradeoff when scaling to larger models, dropping to a poor (bottom 10%) rating for text generation with a 70B parameter model. The high memory density and integrated 1890 GB NVMe SSD make it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy applications and local caching, though it is less optimal for massive parallel compute or large-scale AI inference.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized server instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores running at 4.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 256.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core) and a 1890 GB local NVMe SSD. Benchmarks show top-tier (top 10%) single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations rank in the average tier, while PassMark CPU and encryption scores are strong (top 25%). The instance is highly efficient for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, and single-threaded tasks. However, it exhibits a performance tradeoff for large-scale LLM inference, where text generation speeds for a 70B model fall into the bottom 10%. It is best suited for relational databases, caching layers, and enterprise workloads requiring high memory density and fast local storage.
